scopeLimits: The WUP point is a population-cluster locator, not an official city boundary or parcel identity. TKGM provides single-point identify and exact-ID lookup, not area enumeration through this adapter. Geometry confirms parcels only at queried points; no citywide completeness or WUP coverage is inferred. No owner/address/personal data were saved.

pointBasis: UN WUP 2025 population-weighted settlement centroid; this is not a municipal boundary or a parcel-coverage claim.
registryBasis: Official TKGM point lookups returned complete parcel polygons at nine nearby Bursa sample points; Bursa Metropolitan Municipality also documents a municipal parcel/address viewer. The WUP point and separately selected central sample locator were no-hits; citywide coverage is unqualified.

coverageAssessment.claimedScope: Point query only; Bursa citywide extent is not claimed.
coverageAssessment.verifiedOpenScope: Full polygons returned for 9 of 13 explicit point probes; exact-ID queries returned matching geometry hashes. The WUP and selected central points were no-hits.

research.blocker: TKGM provides point identify and exact-ID lookup but rejects bounds/geometry queries with 422 before network access. One of nine sampled polygons self-intersects in native and EPSG:32635 coordinates; no geometry repair was applied. Citywide parcel completeness remains unqualified.
research.remainingUncertainty: The WUP locator and separately chosen central locator returned structured no-hits; nine nearby sample locations returned complete polygons. No official boundary, area-enumeration endpoint, or parcel count is available from this adapter. One sampled source polygon is topologically invalid.

verifiedParcelResponse.adapterPointNoHitCaveat: Four provider 404s at point locations are returned as structured empty results after strict decimal-comma normalization; they are not network errors or citywide absences.

runtimeAssessment.reason: Nine full public parcel polygons pass point and exact-ID retrieval with matching hashes, and structured point no-hits now work. One polygon self-intersects in a fresh native WGS84 reread and the projected audit; no repair or undocumented exclusion was applied. Point lookup has no area enumeration, which is a capability limitation rather than the quality hold.
